[RLOW.4.5.2.1] **A pure `let` is inlined.** The compiler must substitute a
pure `let`'s right-hand side, with any earlier `let` it names already
substituted, at every use, and lower the result as any expression
([RLOW.6]). A pure `let` produces no atom, no node and no bind slot. A pure
expression used at N sites is evaluated N times: inlined, not memoised
([LLET.10.3]).
